Alright well I just did our weekly group last night and it was a great session which concluded an impromptu dungeon our DM came up with while we were going off on a rabbit trail from the main plot :). Our group of six adventurers were making their way through Baldur's Gate on a mission from the Order of the Gauntlet (HotDQ) when our literature-collecting wizard spotted what was most certainly a powerful wizard's tower. He attempted to gain entrance on his own but there were two guards standing out front who wouldn't let him in and he couldn't take them by himself even if he wanted to; for the time being, the tower was left untouched.

A few hours later our group had some time to kill so we decided to all go to the tower and see if we could find a way to be granted an audience by the powerful wizard. On the way there we concocted the plan to pose as a tourist group who had express permission to see all rooms of the tower as well as the surrounding gardens. I, being the fast-talking one of the group, gladly took the role of the tour guide and spent a few minutes jotting down some notes and random factoids to spat out for the guards to hear. And so, we enacted our plan and I marched them around the gardens talking about random flowers and things while giving out some "facts" about the tower. After a few minutes of the guards not seeming to mind what we were doing, I told everyone in the group that we would now head into the tower and march directly to the door.

The guards (obviously) stopped us and said that no one was allowed in. I responded (acting surprised that we were not just allowed to walk in) that I was from the Baldur's Gate Tourism Department and that this was the final stop in the Baldur's Gate Towers tour: they must be confused or something as we should be allowed in. The others played their part well, acting annoyed and complaining about the tour not going as planned. We were on track to pull this off and it just might work...

The head guard asked a few questions but ultimately decided that he must go talk to the wizard about this whole tourism thing because he wasn't informed of it. Assuming that our scheme was about to be undone, and seeing that the door was now open, I nonchalantly walked in right after him and ushered the group to follow. The second guard held up his hand but before the DM could get out what he wanted to say I high-fived him, smiled like an idiot, and kept walking in... yeah, we all got hit by a magic missile. Still not breaking character, we all made a huge fuss about how terrible the tour was going and demanding better treatment. The head guard turned around and told us we had to leave right now.

Obviously we weren't going to give up that easily so our monk decided to beat the crap out of the first guard who attacked us and then our ranger, in a rare bloodthirsty moment, leaped over the group from the back and plunged a dagger into his throat. What ensued next was a rather comical battle where half our group was trying to run away and the other was dead set on getting into the tower. Eventually, and against all odds (and the DM's intentions), we managed to down all the guards and popped our heads into the tower. The door shut behind us, and a pedestal with a map appeared near the stairs leading upwards into the tower where there was a single door. We decided to take a short rest and then proceeded on a wild portal-world dungeon adventure which left us all with several new character features and an alignment change or two but we managed to make it to the final room after a few sessions worth of turmoil.

We walked through the final portal and came upon a mostly empty room covered in dust. There was a desk with a note and a chest in the corner. The note read something like this:

To the captain of the guard,
I am going on a three-year fishing trip and have left some of my most prized possession in this chest. Guard it and the tower well and do not, under any circumstances, let anyone inside the tower for any reason at all.
Sincerely,
Ramazith

P.S. make an exception for the Baldur's Gate Tourism Department. What is the point of having this wonderful tower and beautiful gardens if no one ever gets to see them!
